reference_sql:
SELECT s.country_code, ROUND(AVG(t.n_orders), 2) AS avg_orders
FROM (
  -- one row per store with orders
  SELECT store_id, COUNT(*) AS n_orders
  FROM orders
  GROUP BY store_id
) AS t
JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = t.store_id
GROUP BY s.country_code
alternatives:
SELECT s.country_code, ROUND(COUNT(*) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT o.store_id), 2) AS avg_orders
FROM orders o
JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id
GROUP BY s.country_code

WITH store_orders AS (
  -- one row per store with orders
  SELECT store_id, COUNT(*) AS n_orders
  FROM orders
  GROUP BY store_id
)
SELECT s.country_code, ROUND(AVG(so.n_orders), 2) AS avg_orders
FROM store_orders so
JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = so.store_id
GROUP BY s.country_code

other_way.sql:
SELECT s.country_code, ROUND(COUNT(*) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT o.store_id), 2) AS avg_orders
FROM orders o
JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id
GROUP BY s.country_code
other_way.tradeoff: Dividing the orders by the distinct stores of each country needs no inner step, but hides the per-store counts.
